newsitem.title: FRANCE: Former premier blames Rwanda for refugee crisis.
newsitem.headline: Former premier blames Rwanda for refugee crisis.

text.p: Rwanda's former Hutu Prime Minister blamed the country's Tutsi-led government on Wednesday for the refugee crisis in East Zaire.
"The refugees are not going back because inside the country there are very serious problems," Faustin Twagiramungu told a news conference at the European Parliament.
He said the government had been responsible for "growing disappearances and arbitrary arrests" when refugees started to return to Rwanda in 1994 after the intervention of French troops.
He said Kigali was exaggerating the problem of the presence among the refugees of armed Hutu militias responsible for the genocide in 1994 to hide its own responsibility for the problems.
More than a million long-term Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees are cut off from all aid in eastern Zaire by a conflict between Zairean troops and Tutsi rebels, who hold much of the region.
Thousands are feared to be dying on mountains and in the jungle.
